title: TypeScript Generics: Type-Safe APIs, Constraints & Variance
description: Master advanced TypeScript generics: constrained type parameters, generic inference, variance (covariance/contravariance), conditional type branching, and building fully type-safe API clients and utility factories.

data.text: Generics: TypeScript's Most Powerful Abstraction Mechanism

TypeScript generics are parameterized types that allow functions, classes, and interfaces to operate on a family of types while preserving full compile-time type safety. Unlike C# generics which have runtime reification, TypeScript generics are erased at compile time—they exist solely to guide the type checker. In enterprise AI frontend code, generics power type-safe API clients, universal hook factories, discriminated response containers, and middleware pipelines.

data.text: Constrained Generics with keyof and extends

Generic constraints narrow the set of types a type parameter accepts, enabling safe property access without runtime guards. The `keyof` operator combined with indexed access types (`T[K]`) creates compile-time verified property lookup utilities.

data.text: TypeScript's type inference can automatically resolve generic type parameters from function arguments, return types, and contextual types—eliminating the need for explicit type annotations in most call sites.

data.caption: Covariance vs Contravariance: The Direction of Type Compatibility
rows: A type is covariant if a subtype can be used where the supertype is expected
Return types of functions, readonly array members
Promise<Cat> is assignable to Promise<Animal> when Cat extends Animal
A type is contravariant if the supertype can be used where the subtype is expected
Function parameter types, event handler callbacks
A handler for Animal events can safely handle Cat events (accepts the broader supertype)
Neither covariance nor contravariance applies; types must match exactly
MutableArray<Cat> is NOT assignable to MutableArray<Animal> — mutation would allow pushing a Dog

data.title: TypeScript Generics Mastery Checklist
items: Use Result<T, E> discriminated unions instead of throwing errors across async API boundaries
Apply keyof and T[K] constraints to guarantee compile-time property access safety
Prefer generic inference over explicit type annotations to keep call sites readable
Mark read-only generic containers with readonly to enable covariant subtype assignment
Use the infer keyword inside conditional types to extract deeply nested type information
Test complex generic utilities with type-level tests using @ts-expect-error assertions

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Generic Result<T,E> types enforce structured error handling without try-catch boilerplate.
keyof and indexed access types enable compile-time verified property access on generic objects.
TypeScript's inference engine eliminates verbose explicit type annotations at most call sites.
Next, we explore Utility Types (Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, ReturnType) for type transformation.
data.takeaway: TypeScript generics are the backbone of reusable enterprise code: they preserve type safety across boundaries while enabling APIs that work with any compliant type.
